source.title: GULP: a prediction-based metric between representations
source.authors: Enric Boix-Adserà; Hannah Lawrence; G. Stepaniants; P. Rigollet

record.tranche_reason: Uses GULP, a different representation-distance measure, to test whether similarities between independently trained networks change with training and model width.
record.gate_note: The paper measures representation distances and reports results for training, width, regularization settings, and input-data changes. It does not test cross-modal alignment, whether representations can be mapped between models, or recurrence of interpretable features. Architecture clustering alone is not treated as evidence for those versions.
record.test_reason: A metrics paper (GULP) whose own results bear on the claim in two ways. First, it reports how distances between independently initialized networks evolve over training and with width. Second, it shows that whether that convergence appears depends on the metric and on λ. It is not one of the original sources.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors' main conclusion is that GULP is a theoretically grounded distance that tracks linear-predictor generalization and separates architecture families. On convergence, they say that at larger λ the distance between independently trained networks decreases during training, which they take as capturing intrinsic properties rather than seed artifacts, whereas other metrics barely change. They also say wider same-depth MLPs converge to a shared limiting representation, and that architecture clustering does not strongly depend on the input distribution.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a prediction-based GULP distance rather than the methods of the cited original convergence studies; the comparisons here focus on GULP's behavior across architectures, width, training, and input distributions.
record.method_sensitivity: GULP outcomes vary with regularization λ: small values accentuate differences, while larger values yield smoother training-time decreases and stronger cross-model grouping of later BERT layers. The architecture clustering result is reported as persisting across ImageNet, MNIST, and UTKFace representation inputs.

fits_no_version.finding: GULP architecture-family clustering of 37 ImageNet models persists when the representations are computed on MNIST or UTKFace inputs. Families also cluster when the networks are untrained (Fig 15).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representational similarity structure between models is organized by architecture family, largely independent of input distribution and partly present at initialization.

record.problems: The claim-relevant convergence results are largely qualitative descriptions of figures, with no numerical trajectory values or uncertainty estimates stated in the text. Width experiments do not measure capability. The results are limited to the tested architectures, tasks, metrics, and datasets.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for every plotted GULP λ or every comparator metric: the text summarizes these outcomes in groups, while the figures' individual numerical values are not described in the text. Static architecture-clustering results on ImageNet and the linear-probing benchmarks were omitted because they do not report outcomes on a claim version beyond the specific width, training, metric-sensitivity, and input-distribution findings recorded above.

untested.parts: Models differing in architecture, objective or data; capability rather than width; larger-scale models.
Not tested: no vision-language paired data.
Not tested: no mapping or stitching between models, though GULP is itself a linear-predictor-based distance.
Not tested: no interpretable features or circuits.
Neighbour-count settings; input or out-of-distribution dependence of convergence itself (input tests concern only architecture clustering).
Not tested: neither plateaus nor explanations via shared data or objectives.

missing.what: MNIST MLP width experiment under GULP λ=1e-6: large-width, small-depth networks are the most different (the 'halo'), organized by feature rank. This is the opposite of the λ=1e-2 convergence trend.
Repeat of the width-depth experiment on CIFAR10 MLPs (μP training). Distance matrices and MDS plots are shown, but no convergence statement is given in the text.

record.verdict_notes: This is primarily a metric-design paper, so its convergence evidence is qualitative and figure-based, with no uncertainty estimates. The input-distribution results (r7, r8) concern clustering by architecture, not convergence, so the record's V6 'challenges' label has been dropped.

versions.untested_parts: Tests widening same-depth MNIST fully connected networks, but not increasing capability or convergence across models with different objectives, training data, or modalities.
Measures representation-distance trends across independent seeds; does not identify specific shared features or subspaces.
Does not test mapping, stitching, relative representations, or unpaired alignment between models.
Does not test recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits.
Tests sensitivity to GULP regularization, comparison metrics, and input data in the reported settings; does not test neighbour-count settings or broad out-of-distribution effects.
Does not establish whether alignment plateaus or remains far from complete, or compare shared-data/objective explanations against a common-reality explanation.

rows.subject: fully-connected ReLU networks (aggregate)
rows.size_stated: Widths 100 to 1,000; depths 1 to 10; four random initializations per architecture
rows.operation_detail: Compared GULP distances across width and depth settings
rows.measure: Pairwise representation distances, visualized with MDS
rows.value: Networks of the same depth look most similar at larger widths; the authors say this suggests convergence toward a shared limiting representation as width increases.
rows.note: Aggregate description of the width-depth experiment; this is a within-family width trend, not a capability sweep.
rows.check: Holds for GULP λ=1e-2 and Procrustes: same-depth MLPs look most similar at large widths. This is within one family on MNIST with one objective, so it does not test different architectures, data or objectives. At λ=1e-6 the pattern differs (see missing). The state is for V1 under λ=1e-2/Procrustes. Qualitative and figure-based.

rows.subject: 16 independently trained ResNet18 architectures (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Tracked average pairwise GULP distance over training

conditions.value: GULP with small λ; specific values not stated in the text summary

rows.measure: Average pairwise representation distance, normalized by its average value at iteration 0
rows.value: Small λ accentuates representation differences during training, including around epoch 25; the displayed distance trajectory is figure-only.
rows.note: The text describes the small-λ behavior qualitatively; the plotted numerical values are not transcribed.
rows.check: Small-λ GULP shows differences between seeds accentuated mid-training (around epoch 25), not a smooth convergence. For V3 this is partial. Its V6 relevance is the contrast with r3 and r4.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4.3; Figure 7 caption; Appendix B.7 and Figure 19 caption.

rows.subject: 16 independently trained ResNet18 architectures (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Tracked average pairwise GULP distance over training

conditions.value: GULP with larger λ; specific values not stated in the text summary

rows.measure: Average pairwise representation distance, normalized by its average value at iteration 0
rows.value: As λ increases, GULP distinguishes the representations less and decreases smoothly during training; the plotted numerical values are figure-only.
rows.note: Shows a decreasing distance across training, but the text does not report distances reaching zero or complete identity.
rows.check: Larger-λ GULP between 16 ResNet18 seeds decreases smoothly over training. The size of the drop is figure-only (Fig 7/19) and cannot be read from the text.

rows.subject: CCA, PWCCA, Linear CKA, and PROCRUSTES distances (aggregate as described in text)
rows.operation_detail: Compared alternative representation distances over training
rows.measure: Average pairwise representation distance over training
rows.value: The other distances change very little or briefly increase during training.
rows.note: The paper gives this as an aggregate textual description rather than separate textual outcomes for each comparator metric.
rows.check: Role is mislabeled as comparator. These are measurements of the same seed-convergence phenomenon under CCA, PWCCA, linear CKA and Procrustes, which change very little or briefly increase.

rows.subject: 10 BERT base models (aggregate)
rows.stage_stated: pretrained with different random initializations on MNLI
rows.operation_detail: Measured GULP distances between hidden-layer representations across models
rows.measure: Pairwise representation distance, visualized as distance matrices and embeddings
rows.value: At small λ, earlier layers across the models group together, while later layers have large distances between models; numerical distances are figure-only.
rows.note: The described grouping is layer-dependent and does not establish shared individual features.
rows.check: At small λ, early layers group across the 10 BERT seeds but later layers stay far apart.

rows.subject: 37 pretrained ImageNet models (aggregate)
rows.size_stated: Representation dimensions range from 400 to 4096, depending on architecture
rows.operation_detail: Compared GULP-based architecture clustering when representations were computed on MNIST inputs

conditions.value: 10,000 MNIST training images converted to RGB and normalized

rows.measure: Pairwise representation distances and architecture clustering
rows.baseline: Clustering of representations computed from ImageNet training images
rows.value: EfficientNet, ResNet, and ConvNeXt architectures remain separately clustered; the authors say the metric does not strongly depend on the input distribution in this experiment.
rows.note: This is evidence against strong input-distribution dependence for this architecture-clustering result.
rows.check: Measures whether architecture-family clustering persists when the inputs are MNIST. It does not measure convergence between models or how convergence changes with inputs, so it should not bear on V6.

rows.value: The models again cluster by architecture family; the authors describe the metric as not overly sensitive to the input distribution in these examples.
